contentHtml:
Mumbai: Global pharmaceutical company Lupin Limited has launched Sugammadex Injection in the United States following approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (USFDA) for its Abbreviated New Drug Application (ANDA).

In a regulatory filing, the company said it has introduced Sugammadex Injection, 200 mg/2 mL and 500 mg/5 mL single-dose vials in the U.S. market.

Lupin said the product is bioequivalent and therapeutically equivalent to BRIDION (Sugammadex) Injection of Merck Sharp & Dohme LLC.

The injection is indicated for the reversal of neuromuscular blockade induced by rocuronium bromide and vecuronium bromide in adults and pediatric patients aged 2 years and older undergoing surgery.

The launch follows the recent USFDA approval of Lupin's ANDA for the product, expanding the company's portfolio of injectable medicines in the U.S.
